#1 In this article it says that the groupoid cardinality of the 2D hypercomplex number systems is 32\frac 3 223​ because there are three 2D hypercomplex number systems (up to isomorphism) each equipped with one non-trivial algebra automorphism. But surely, the dual numbers have infinitely many automorphisms satisfying 1↦1,ϵ↦kϵ1 \mapsto 1, \epsilon \mapsto k\epsilon1↦1,ϵ↦kϵ (where kkk is an arbitrary non-zero real number), so the value of the groupoid cardinality is actually 12+12+1∞=1\frac 1 2 + \frac 1 2 + \frac 1 \infty = 121​+21​+∞1​=1.

Who is right?

#3 I haven’t thought about what the entry claims (or even looked at it until a minute ago), but, in response to David:

The operation ϕk\phi_kϕk​ : 1↦11 \mapsto 11↦1 and ϵ↦kϵ\epsilon \mapsto k \epsilonϵ↦kϵ for k∈R∖{0}k \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}k∈R∖{0} is certainly an automorphism of the ring of dual numbers R[ϵ]/(ϵ2)\mathbb{R}[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)R[ϵ]/(ϵ2):

Explicitly, check that

ϕk(1+aϵ)⋅ϕk(1+bϵ)=  (1+kaϵ)(1+kbϵ)=  (1+k(a+b)ϵ)=  ϕk(1+(a+b)ϵ)=  ϕk((1+aϵ)⋅(1+bϵ)) \begin{aligned} \phi_k(1 + a \epsilon) \cdot \phi_k(1 + b \epsilon) & =\; (1 + k a \epsilon) (1 + k b \epsilon) \\ & =\; (1 + k (a + b) \epsilon) \\ & =\; \phi_k\big( 1 + (a + b) \epsilon \big) \\ & =\; \phi_k\big( (1 + a \epsilon) \cdot (1 + b \epsilon) \big) \end{aligned} ϕk​(1+aϵ)⋅ϕk​(1+bϵ)​=(1+kaϵ)(1+kbϵ)=(1+k(a+b)ϵ)=ϕk​(1+(a+b)ϵ)=ϕk​((1+aϵ)⋅(1+bϵ))​

More conceptually, notice that (Hadamard's lemma)

R[ϵ]/(ϵ2)  ≃  C∞(R)/(ϵ2) \mathbb{R}[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2) \;\simeq\; C^\infty(\mathbb{R})/(\epsilon^2) R[ϵ]/(ϵ2)≃C∞(R)/(ϵ2)

so that every diffeomorphism of R\mathbb{R}R which fixes the origin induces an automorphism of R[ϵ]/(ϵ2)\mathbb{R}[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)R[ϵ]/(ϵ2) (given by the diffeomorphism’s first Taylor coefficient, which is the kkk from above).

content: #8 Regarding the claim that the perplex numbers have precisely two automorphisms, this is true. First, it’s easy to see that ϕ1(a+be)=a+be\phi_1(a + \mathrm{be}) = a + \mathrm{be}ϕ1​(a+be)=a+be and ϕ2(a+be)=a−be\phi_2(a + \mathrm{be}) = a - \mathrm{be}ϕ2​(a+be)=a−be are two distinct automorphisms. It remains to prove that all automorphisms over the perplex numbers are of this form. Let ϕ\phiϕ be an automorphism over the perplex numbers. Observe that ϕ(e)2=ϕ(e2)=ϕ(1)=1\phi(e)^2 = \phi(e^2) = \phi(1) = 1ϕ(e)2=ϕ(e2)=ϕ(1)=1. It follows that ϕ(e)∈{1,−1,e,−e}\phi(e) \in \{1,-1,e,-e\}ϕ(e)∈{1,−1,e,−e}. But if ϕ(e)∈{+1,−1}\phi(e) \in \{+1, -1\}ϕ(e)∈{+1,−1} then ϕ\phiϕ is not injective. So therefore ϕ(e)∈{e,−e}\phi(e) \in \{e, -e\}ϕ(e)∈{e,−e}.
